description_full: FMC Corporation, an agricultural sciences company, develops, markets, and sells crop protection chemicals in Latin America, North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. The company offers crop protection chemicals, including insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides. It also provides biologicals, crop nutrition, and seed treatment products. It markets its products through its sales organization and alliance partners, independent distributors, and sales representatives. The company was founded in 1883 and is headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: FMC Corporation is a small-cap basic materials business with a $876M market cap on $3.5B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -16% over the past three years and +1% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -3.7pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 38%.
The company is burning through $102M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at -23.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, thin -6.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 33.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 21% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
